question: With the same VM v1.134 release and fixed complete read-only indexed data, when is per-day tag index search cheaper than global tag index search for 1/3 day PromQL?
baseline: VM v1.134.0 optimized SHA-pinned release and default per-day index search on stored data; TagFilters index-cache budget fixed to 1 byte
candidate: Exactly same binary and physical indexed base snapshot, -disablePerDayIndex=true forces global search; TagFilters cache budget unchanged at 1 byte
fixture: Exact R01 aligned 400-slot 3d 2,488,320 sample/28,896 series SHA256 ea9a8d43c9e58ed916f1bf43949556d8ed18169ddd14033c293af4cd54c9881d
single_variable: VM index read path selection via -disablePerDayIndex in fresh VM processes, not data ingestion or cache capacity
math_bound: Per-day performs D date posting lookups and unions; global performs one posting lookup spanning all retained series. For small D and churned data expected postings inspected N_day << N_global, but cost of union/seek and page cache can cross over. D bounded by actual query and partition.
falsifier: Different native labels/timestamps/values, metrics/trace showing same effective path, baseline A/A drift >=25%, OOM, background cache resets or clone mismatch
test_matrix: VM global/day/day/global same-host ABBA with clean post-ingest data clones, 1 byte TagFilter cache for both, 8 warmups+48 measured single-client requests per 4 selectors, one-tick and three-tick 1d ranges, per-query trace and CPU/RSS; exact output parity
runner_budget: Single GitHub-hosted Ubuntu24.04 runner; reuse verified VM v1.134 artifact, no build, timeout 65min, self-path workflow push only, do not cancel existing jobs
overlap_note: Distinct from R25 cache capacity test, E03/R06 CH optimizer, R05 marks, R07 day metadata; source feature test of VM index read-path only
